name: Moorebot Scout
description: A Kickstarter-origin, Mecanum-wheeled home patrol robot marketed toward developers with Linux + ROS 1 access. Marketed autonomous SLAM mapping and full open APIs were, per independent developer reports, never fully delivered.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: ~2 hr runtime; auto-dock unreliable per reviewers

specs.label: Software
specs.note: not ROS 2; control layer open-sourced only

specs.label: Navigation
specs.note: marketed as "SLAM"; true SLAM never shipped per developers

specs.label: Modularity
specs.note: plow, laser pointer, cat wand — sold separately

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: local storage (onboard flash/FTP-NAS) always free; cloud storage & push notifications need a monthly sub after a 3-month free trial — price not published

sourcing: Verified against Moorebot's own official site and FAQ (moorebot.com), the original Kickstarter campaign, Hackster.io's launch coverage, independent developer/enthusiast reports (We Speak IoT), and direct inspection of Pilot Labs' official open-source control-layer repo (confirmed MIT license) and the separate third-party community ROS driver project (confirmed Apache-2.0, confirmed unaffiliated). This page reports both the manufacturer's marketing claims and the independently-reported gap between those claims and real-world SLAM/ROS 2 functionality, since that gap is material to anyone evaluating this as a security device rather than a hobbyist toy. No mainstream tech-press review was found for this product.

pricing.summary: Officially listed at **$199.99** (down from $219.99) on Moorebot's own site, which currently shows the product as sold out; also sold through Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware — Claims vs. Reality
editorial.body: The drive system is as advertised: four Mecanum wheels give true omnidirectional movement, clearing 15mm obstacles and 25° slopes. But marketing overstates the rest: it implies SLAM-style autonomous mapping, yet independent developer reports say full SLAM was never shipped — the robot only records rough pre-driven paths. Marketing also suggests ROS 2 support, but Moorebot's FAQ confirms only ROS 1.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Moorebot markets Scout's navigation as SLAM-style autonomous mapping with 24/7 patrol capability, but independent developer reports confirm true SLAM was never shipped — it only follows rough pre-driven paths and often fails to find its own charging dock. Marketing also implies full ROS 2 access, but Moorebot's own FAQ confirms the platform runs ROS 1, not ROS 2.

firmwareCommunity.note: Moorebot's own official open-source repository for Scout, covering its recognition and extension-framework code (the robot's core communication layer itself stays closed for security reasons).
